Mesh & Resolution(M. Falk, PE); External Standards Digest(M. Falk, PE).
--- PAGE 2 ---
the run identifier from which S is taken. Descriptive words such as "matches," "agrees," "confirms," or "is validated"
are inadmissible substitutes for the numerical statement. The reviewing engineer shall reject any submitted
deliverable that omits any of the four quantities or that replaces the numerical rollup with a qualitative
characterization.
The requirement to report E with u_val — rather than a binary outcome — is not a matter of firm style. A yes/no
verdict conceals the sign and magnitude of the discrepancy, hides whether the disagreement is within measurement
scatter or resolved as a model error, and forecloses the diagnostic reasoning the validation exercise exists to support.
The reviewing engineer shall enforce the reporting form on every deliverable.
4. Uncertainty Build-Up
The validation uncertainty u_val is the root-sum-square (RSS) combination of three independent components, each
expressed in the units of the quantity being validated:
1. Numerical uncertainty, u_num. Reflects discretization, iterative convergence, and round-off contributions in S.
For the class of problem addressed in Section 8 — a conjugate thermal simulation of a compartment-wall assembly
under an ASTM E119 exposure — the firm's default value is ±4 min, established from prior three-grid conjugate
thermal studies on similar assemblies. A project-specific value shall be substituted where a resolution study or
convergence study supports one. 2. Input uncertainty, u_inp. Reflects propagation of uncertainties in material
properties (temperature-dependent conductivity, density, specific heat), boundary conditions (furnace-side
temperature histories, ambient side convective and radiative loss), and geometric idealization (leaf thickness, tie
diameter and spacing, cavity dimension). The firm's default value for the same class of problem is ±6 min. 3.
Experimental uncertainty, u_exp. Reflects instrument, calibration, and placement contributions to D as reported by
the testing laboratory. For calibrated Type-K thermocouples of the class used in ASTM E119 furnace work, the firm's
default value is ±5 min.
Combining by root-sum-square:
 u_val = sqrt( u_num^2 + u_inp^2 + u_exp^2 )
= sqrt( 4^2 + 6^2 + 5^2 )
= sqrt( 16 + 36 + 25 )
= sqrt( 77 )
= ±8.77 min
The result is reported to whole minutes: u_val = ±9 min for this class of problem.
Two guardrails apply.
First, the three components must be independent. If the numerical model uses lab-measured material properties
whose uncertainty is already folded into D, that property uncertainty shall not be double-counted in u_inp. The
reviewing engineer shall verify independence at the peer review stage.
Second, the default values shall be reviewed at least annually or whenever a project uses a materially different
assembly, exposure, or instrument class. A project-specific tabulation of u_num, u_inp, u_exp shall be recorded in
the project QA folder before u_val is published.
5. Acceptance Criterion
The firm acceptance criterion is |E| ≤ 10% of D.
The criterion is scaled: it grows with the endurance value being validated, so short endurances demand tighter
agreement in absolute minutes and long endurances tolerate more. A 30-minute endurance carries a 3-minute band;
a 120-minute endurance carries a 12-minute band; a 240-minute endurance carries a 24-minute band. This scaling is
deliberate. Absolute-minute criteria are unstable across the range of assemblies the firm analyzes; a 5-minute
absolute tolerance is loose against a 30-minute rating and severe against a 4-hour rating. A percentage-of-D criterion
is stable across the range and disciplines short-endurance work where the absolute stakes are largest.
Two secondary tests accompany the primary criterion and shall appear in every validation rollup:
  Compare |E| to u_val. If |E| ≤ u_val, the discrepancy is within the combined validation uncertainty and is best
characterized as measurement-plus-model scatter. If |E| > u_val, the discrepancy is resolved as a model error —
larger than the noise floor of the exercise — and shall be treated as an actionable finding, regardless of whether

--- PAGE 3 ---
the primary 10% criterion is met.
 Compare the sign of E to the direction of the physical expectation. A simulation that consistently over-predicts
endurance carries different engineering implications from one that consistently under-predicts; the sign is
preserved in every rollup and discussed in the report narrative.
A deliverable in which |E| exceeds the criterion, or in which |E| exceeds u_val, or both, shall not be released with an
unqualified validation claim. The reviewing engineer determines whether the deliverable may be released with a
documented finding, whether the model shall be reworked, or whether the validation reference itself is unsuitable and
a different reference shall be sought.
6. Source of D
D shall be taken from the certified third-party test report of record. Client-amended values may not be
substituted for D absent a reissued report from the testing laboratory of record and a calibration certificate authorizing
the revision. Post-test amendments transmitted by the client but not authorized by the lab are not admissible as D.
The rule is strict for a reason. D is the physical anchor of the validation; if D moves for any reason other than a
documented laboratory action, the validation ceases to be against the physical test and becomes a comparison
against a preferred number. The two states are indistinguishable in the report if the substitution is silent, and the
record of the exercise is corrupted.
The following forms of documentation are required to substitute a revised D:
1. A reissued report from the testing laboratory of record, bearing the same report number as the original with an
amendment sequence (e.g., "-R1"), signed by the laboratory's authorized signatory, and stating the reason for the
revision. 2. A calibration certificate covering the instrument or measurement whose revision is at issue, with a date
and calibration-authority reference sufficient to trace the correction. 3. An explicit statement, in the reissued report,
that the revised value supersedes the value in the original report for all downstream use.
Absent any of the three, the original value stands. The reviewing engineer shall reject any deliverable that draws D
from a client-amended figure not backed by the above documentation. A polite, specific, thermocouple-calibration
explanation transmitted by a client is not a laboratory revision; the analyst shall record the client transmittal in the
correspondence folder and continue to use the certified D. Any pressure to depart from this rule — from schedule,
from commercial positioning, or from a persuasive account of what "really" happened at the test — shall be resolved
by returning to the reissued-report requirement.
7. Scope Limitation
ASTM E119 exposes an assembly to the standard building time-temperature curve, which is not a WUI
wildfire exposure. E119 endurance is therefore a comparative assembly rating, not a prediction of wildfire survival
time. Validation against E119 data validates the model against E119; it does not validate a wildfire performance
claim.
The distinction is not a formality. The E119 curve is a smooth, monotonically rising fuel-continuous compartment fire
scenario intended to grade the relative thermal performance of building assemblies under a repeatable exposure. A
wildland-urban interface exposure is a wind-driven, radiation-dominated, transient fire-front event whose peak heat
flux, duration, and spatial distribution differ from E119 at every axis. An assembly with a two-hour E119 rating is not
thereby a two-hour wildfire assembly, and no algebraic manipulation of an E119 result yields a wildfire survival time.
Firm practice on this point:
  Reports that use E119 test data to validate a CFD model shall state, in the validation section, that the validation
exercise establishes model fidelity against the E119 exposure and shall not extrapolate that finding to wildfire,
hydrocarbon-pool, or other non-E119 exposures.
 Where a project's ultimate objective is a wildfire performance claim, the validation section shall separately identify
(i) what E119 data validates, (ii) what it does not, and (iii) what additional physical evidence would be required to
close the gap.
 Marketing or commercial statements that translate an E119 rating into a wildfire performance figure are outside
the firm's stamp and shall not appear in any firm-issued deliverable.

[Normal] 1.1 Purpose
[Normal] This report documents the Phase 1 thermal-CFD analysis of the Ocotillo Additive Structures double-wythe printed-concrete cavity wall assembly under Sonoran Desert wildland-urban-interface exposure. The analysis is a large-eddy simulation of a fire-front segment representative of a Sonoran buffelgrass surface fire advancing on the exposed face of the assembly. The exposure envelope, fire-source characterisation, mesh study, and preliminary thermal response are reported here. Companion structural wind-pressure work under SOW Section 3.2 is documented separately.
[Normal] 1.2 Scope
[Normal] The scope of the Phase 1 analysis is limited to:
[List Bullet] Regime classification and selection of solver stack;
[List Bullet] Site-envelope characterisation from Pima County ALERT ten-year hourly meteorology;
[List Bullet] Fire-source characterisation from published Rothermel / Byram / solid-flame correlations for the specified fuel model;
[List Bullet] Large-eddy simulation of the fire-front sub-domain at design-envelope wind speeds and directions;
[List Bullet] Thermal treatment of the double-wythe cavity wall assembly per the project case-setup record;
[List Bullet] Verification of the LES discretisation on the wildfire sub-domain;
[List Bullet] Preliminary reporting of unexposed-face and tie-embedded thermal response.
[Normal] 1.3 Scope exclusions
[Normal] Fire-resistance rating certification of the assembly is explicitly outside the scope of this report and outside the stamp boundary of The CFD ME. The certified rating for the subject wall assembly is issued separately by others (see the standard stamp block in §9). This report is a computational thermal analysis; it does not certify, extend, or modify any assembly rating.
[Normal] Structural wind-pressure work per SOW §3.2 is a separate deliverable and is not included here.

[Normal] THE CFD ME   |   Tucson, Arizona   |   AZ PE #48213   |   CFDME-2025-041 rev A
[Normal] MEMORANDUM — PHASE 1 SCOPING
[Normal] 1.  Purpose & Scope
[Normal] This memo fixes, at project kickoff and before any meshing is undertaken, the first-principles basis on which the Phase 1 wildfire-exposure large-eddy simulation set will be built. It records the design conditions taken from the site meteorological pull, the buffelgrass fuel model, the Rothermel-to-Byram source-term chain that produces the design fire, the Froude regime assessment inputs, and the LES sub-domain geometry against which downstream mesh sizing will be measured. It is issued on the effective date of the Ocotillo Additive Structures Phase 1 Statement of Work (CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01, signed 10/08/2025), before revC of the assembly geometry (OAS-WUI-01_revC, transmitted with the SOW) is imported into the mesher.
[Normal] The intent is that every downstream case-setup artifact, mesh-study artifact, and Phase 1 reporting deliverable — including the interim hand-calc due 10/13/2025 and the LES setup deliverable due 10/20/2025 — trace their source-term, regime, and geometry inputs back to the numbers recorded here, rather than re-argue them case-by-case. Where a downstream artifact needs the design fire heat release, the characteristic source diameter, or the plume length scale, it shall cite this memo.
[Normal] The scope of Phase 1 as procured under Section 3.1 of the SOW is six transient wildfire cases (240 deg and 270 deg wind directions at 20-ft wind speeds of 5, 8, and 12 m/s). The fire source term and the sub-domain sizing recorded here apply to that entire matrix; they are not per-case parameters.
[Normal] 2.  Site Design Conditions
[Normal] Design conditions are taken from the ten-year hourly record of the Pima County ALERT network for the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson (data pull: site_met_avra_valley_2015-2024.csv, Section 3.1 of the SOW envelope). The following envelope governs Phase 1:
[Normal] These conditions define the site for regime classification (Section 4 below) and for the source-term chain (Section 3 below). They are the same conditions carried into the Phase 1 report; no re-derivation is required.
[Normal] 3.  Fuel Model — Sonoran Buffelgrass at Site Design Conditions
[Normal] The design fire source term is developed under the Rothermel spread-to-Byram intensity chain, evaluated at the site design conditions of Section 2. The buffelgrass fuel model is adopted per the SOW Section 2 definition (“Buffelgrass Fuel Model”). Fuel-model quantities are:
[Normal] •  Fuel load (dry):  w = 0.6 kg/m²
[Normal] •  Low heat of combustion:  h = 18,600 kJ/kg
[Normal] •  Rate of spread at design wind:  R = 0.9 m/s
[Normal] R is the head-fire rate of spread produced by the Rothermel surface-fire spread model for cured buffelgrass at the low-humidity, high-temperature, moderate-wind conditions of Section 2. It is used here as the input to the Byram fireline-intensity relation; the Rothermel-model input parameter tabulation for buffelgrass is on file with the project data pull.
[Normal] Byram’s fireline intensity is the product of the low heat of combustion, the available fuel load per unit area, and the rate of spread:
[Normal] I = h · w · R
[Normal]   = (18,600 kJ/kg) × (0.6 kg/m²) × (0.9 m/s)
[Normal]   = 10,040 kW/m
[Normal] The Byram wind-tilted solid-flame length correlation gives:
[Normal] L = 0.0775 · I^0.46
[Normal]   = 0.0775 × (10,040)^0.46
[Normal]   = 5.4 m
[Normal] L above is the wind-tilted Byram flame length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height and is not comparable to Heskestad’s still-air correlation (see Section 5 for the idealization record).
[Normal] 4.  Froude / Regime Assessment
[Normal] Regime selection follows CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §2. The controlling non-dimensional group is the Froude number formed on the characteristic source diameter of the LES sub-domain:
[Normal] Fr = u_wind / sqrt(g · D_char)
[Normal] Taking D_char = 3.0 m (the LES sub-domain segment fixed in Section 5 below) and g = 9.81 m/s²:
[Normal] sqrt(g · D_char) = sqrt(9.81 × 3.0) = sqrt(29.43) = 5.42 m/s
[Normal] Evaluated across the site design wind envelope 5–12 m/s:
[Normal] The Froude / plume-velocity ratio falls in the range ~0.9–2.2 across the entire design envelope.
[Normal] Regime classification.  Classification against the Modeling Standard §2 thresholds, and solver selection per §3 of that standard, shall be carried out and documented in the case setup record before any case in this matrix is meshed.
[Normal] This classification is made once, at the firm level, for the entire Phase 1 wildfire matrix; it is not re-argued case-by-case within the envelope.
[Normal] 5.  LES Sub-Domain
[Normal] The LES sub-domain represents a 3.0 m segment of the flaming front. This segment length is the characteristic source width used for the plume model, and the value of D_char used in the Section 4 Froude computation and in the plume-length-scale computation below.
[Normal] 5.1  Line vs Axisymmetric Reconciliation
[Normal] The Byram fireline-intensity relation of Section 3 gives an intensity per unit length of the fire front (kW/m). The plume length scale D* referred to by the firm modeling and verification standards is an axisymmetric-source property (kW total). The two quantities are not interchangeable and cannot be composed directly. The 3.0 m segment length is the specific conversion factor between them for this project: it defines how much fire-front length is captured within one LES sub-domain, and therefore what total heat release rate the plume model sees.
[Normal] Design fire heat release rate for the sub-domain:
[Normal] Q = I × L_segment
[Normal]   = (10,040 kW/m) × (3.0 m)
[Normal]   = 30,120 kW
[Normal]   = 30.1 MW
[Normal] Idealizations recorded so they are not misread as physical dimensions.
[Normal] •  Flame depth and flame residence time are not resolved in this sub-domain. The flaming front is represented as an equivalent 3.0 m characteristic-diameter source patch.
[Normal] •  The wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m from Section 3 is a wind-tilted correlation length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height. Heskestad’s still-air flame-height correlation, evaluated for the same 30.1 MW heat release rate at a 3.0 m diameter source, gives roughly 11.5 m. The 5.4 m vs 11.5 m gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy between two attempts to model the same quantity.
[Normal] Plume characteristic diameter D*.  For Q = 30.1 MW and standard reference-atmosphere conditions (ρ_∞ = 1.204 kg/m³, c_p = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, T_∞ = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s²):
[Normal] D* = ( Q / ( rho_inf · c_p · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^(2/5)
[Normal]    = ( 30,100 / ( 1.204 × 1.005 × 293.15 × 3.132 ) )^(2/5)
[Normal]    = ( 27.08 )^(2/5)
[Normal] D* = 3.76 m.
[Normal] The fine-grid cell size specified for the LES mesh study is dx = 0.5 m (the finest of the three grids in the mesh study). This gives:
[Normal] D* / dx = 3.76 / 0.5 = 7.5
[Normal] which confirms the plume is adequately resolved on the fine grid. LES resolution acceptance shall be assessed per the firm QA standard applicable to reacting-plume LES.
[Normal] 6.  Wall Assembly Note
[Normal] The through-wall response of the assembly cannot be modelled as heat conduction through a single solid slab. Per the OAS-WUI-01_revC wall assembly section (Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png), the assembly is a double-wythe cavity system: two 50 mm printed-concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (overall thickness 305 mm), tied together by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties spaced 600 mm on centre vertically, embedded 25 mm into each leaf. The cavity carries no insulation. The architectural drawing (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW in its title block; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout the SOW, this memo, and all downstream analysis artifacts.
[Normal] The metallic ties are a continuous parallel thermal path between the exposed and unexposed leaves; their conductivity (~45 W/m·K) is more than an order of magnitude above the siliceous-aggregate concrete of the leaves, and they are the reason the single-point criterion governs over the average-rise criterion in the ASTM E119 test result of record.
[Normal] Per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §6, the through-wall modeling treatment for this assembly shall be selected and documented in the case setup record before meshing, accounting for the metallic ties’ thermal-bridge role identified above. Temperature-dependent solid properties (k, ρ, c_p) apply per Modeling Standard §3.5.
[Normal] 7.  Downstream Inputs
[Normal] The following quantities established above are the source-term and length-scale inputs for the downstream Phase 1 case-setup, mesh-study, and reporting artifacts:
[Normal] •  Site design envelope: ambient 35–42 °C, RH 10–25 %, 20-ft wind 5–12 m/s (Section 2).
[Normal] •  Byram fireline intensity I = 10,040 kW/m (Section 3).
[Normal] •  Wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m (Section 3).
[Normal] •  LES sub-domain fire-front segment: 3.0 m (Section 5).
[Normal] •  Design fire heat release rate: 30.1 MW (Section 5.1).
[Normal] •  Plume characteristic diameter: D* = 3.76 m (Section 5.1).
[Normal] •  Froude ratio range across the site design envelope: ~0.9–2.2 (Section 4); regime classification and solver selection per Modeling Standard §§2–3 to be documented in the case setup record (Section 4).
[Normal] •  Wall through-thickness modeling treatment: to be selected and documented per Modeling Standard §6, accounting for the metallic tie thermal-bridge path identified in Section 6.
[Normal] The 3.0 m segment, 30.1 MW source, and D* = 3.76 m established per Section 5 above are the inputs the fine grid dx = 0.5 m recorded in the Meshing and case-build log is sized against.
[Normal] The 5–12 m/s design wind envelope carries forward into the wind-inlet boundary conditions of the six-case matrix, per the solver selection made in Section 4; the puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz predicted by the f = 1.5·D^(-1/2) correlation per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §4 for this plume sets the writeInterval and end-time requirements for each transient run.

This Statement of Work ("SOW") is entered into as of 10/08/2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between The CFD
Mechanical Engineer, LLC, an Arizona limited liability company doing business as The CFD ME, with offices at 4820
E River Rd, Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718 ("Consultant"), and Ocotillo Additive Structures, with offices at 3175 S Palo
Verde Rd, Tucson, AZ 85713 ("Client"). The parties agree as follows.
1. Purpose and Background
Client designs and constructs single-family residential structures using proprietary additive-manufactured (3D-printed)
portland-cement concrete wall assemblies and intends to market those structures for siting within the wildland-urban
interface ("WUI") of the Sonoran Desert west of Tucson, Arizona. Client's marketing programme advances the
positioning that Client's printed-concrete envelope is more fire-resistant, under credible wildfire exposure, than
conventional wood-frame construction of comparable footprint.
Consultant is engaged to provide the computational-fluid-dynamics ("CFD") backing for that positioning as it applies
to a Sonoran Desert buffelgrass wildfire event in the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson. The engagement
covers Phase 1 only: the mixed-convection wildfire plume analyses enumerated in Section 3.1 and the structural
wind-pressure extraction enumerated in Section 3.2, together with the deliverables in Section 4.
Client acknowledges that fire-resistance ratings on the printed wall assembly (including the current 1-hour rating
already issued by others) are outside the scope of this SOW and are certified separately by a third-party
fire-protection engineer under a separate engagement. This SOW procures analysis only.
2. Definitions
For purposes of this SOW, the following terms have the meanings given below.
"Assembly" — the double-wythe printed-concrete wall system, geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC as
transmitted by Client to Consultant on the Effective Date.
"Buffelgrass Fuel Model" — the Sonoran-desert buffelgrass ground-fuel model adopted for the wildfire source term
in the Section 3.1 matrix, as documented in Consultant's Phase 1 scoping memo of even date.
"LES" — large-eddy simulation, meaning transient turbulence-resolving CFD run with wall time-step control per
Consultant's internal modelling standard for reacting buoyant flows.
"Site" — the Avra Valley Sonoran Desert WUI parcel west of Tucson identified in Client's Phase 0 site file.
"Wildfire Matrix" — the six-case matrix of atmospheric conditions and wind directions defined in Section 3.1.
"Structural Wind Case" — the single ASCE 7-22 wind-pressure load case defined in Section 3.2.
"Change Order" — a written amendment to this SOW, executed by both parties, before performance, that modifies
scope, schedule, or fee.
3. Scope of Work
Consultant shall perform the services set out in Sections 3.1 and 3.2 below. Section 3.1 and Section 3.2 are separate
load cases with separate governing bases; results from one shall not be substituted for or compared against results
from the other.

the Site, using Consultant's fireFoam-based LES stack with EDC combustion, fvDOM radiation, and
atmospheric-boundary-layer inlet, per Consultant's internal Modeling Standard for Fire & Buoyant Flows. The matrix
crosses two (2) wind directions with three (3) mean wind speeds at 20 ft reference height, as follows.

Each case shall be run to a physical simulated time covering not fewer than twenty (20) puffing cycles of the plume as

3.2 Structural Wind-Pressure Extraction (ASCE 7-22)
Separately from and independent of the Section 3.1 matrix, Consultant shall extract the design wind pressures on the

 Enclosure classification: enclosed
 Mean roof height: 6.4 m
 Topographic factor K_zt: 1.0
 Ground elevation factor K_e: 1.0
 Directionality factor K_d: 0.85
 Gust-effect factor G: 0.85
 Windward wall pressure coefficient C_p: 0.8
Section 3.2 is a distinct load case, not part of the Section 3.1 matrix. The Section 3.2 result is a code-basis
structural design pressure derived from the ASCE 7-22 procedure with the parameters listed above. It shall not be
substituted for, added to, or interchanged with the wildfire-plume flow-field pressures produced under Section 3.1,
which arise from a different physical regime at different reference wind speeds. Section 3.1 results are transient
plume-flow quantities; the Section 3.2 result is a code-basis design pressure. Consultant shall report each in its own
governing units alongside its governing boundary condition.

steps.message:
I have completed the ASTM E119 companion validation memorandum for Project `CFDME-2025-041` (*Ocotillo WUI Wildfire, Phase 1*) per `CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2.pdf` (`CFDME-QA-VAL-002`, rev 2, effective `05/01/2025`) without modifying any existing file-server records.

### Deliverable Path
- **`output/CFDME-2025-041_validation_memo.docx`** — Formal Word validation memorandum from Gordon Selby, PE (`AZ PE #48213`) to Marguerite Falk, PE (`AZ PE #42798`), dated `10/10/2025`, formatted in firm house style with full units compliance per `CFDME_Units_SOP_rev2.pdf`.

---

### Summary of Key Results

1. **Straight Answer on Validation Status**:
   - **No — the ASTM E119 companion simulation (`E119_companion_sim_results.csv`) does not validate under `CFDME-QA-VAL-002` rev 2 (`ASME V&V 20-2009`), and cannot be described as "validated against the certified test" in Ocotillo's launch materials.**
   - Per `CFDME-QA-VAL-002` §§3–5, the result is reported as **`E ± u_val = +13 min ± 9 min`** (`S = 131 min`, `D = 118 min`, `E = +13 min`, `u_val = ±9 min` [`±8.77 min` exact RSS]), where `|E| = 13 min` exceeds both the primary `10 %` acceptance criterion (`11.8 min`) and the validation uncertainty (`9 min`).

2. **Assembly Identity and Certification Coverage**:
   - **Yes — the assembly in the companion run (`OAS-WUI-01_revC`) is the physical wall assembly covered by Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering Certification Memorandum `IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` (`09/29/2025`, Marla Kettering, PE, `AZ PE #45106`) and tested in Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing Report `RBFMT-25-0918` (`09/24/2025`).**
   - **What that rests on**:
     - *Identifier & Revision Crosswalk*: The dimensioned assembly drawing (`Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png`, Rev A, `09/15/2025`) carries architectural drawing number **`OAS-WA-305mm-DW`**, which designates the exact same physical assembly as the engineering CAD geometry of record **`OAS-WUI-01_revC`** (`Geometry/OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd`, exported `10/08/2025 16:42:11 -0700`, SHA-256 `a4f2c8b91d3e5f7a9c1b2d4e6f8a0c2b5d7e9f1a3c5b7d9e1f3a5c7b9d1e3f5a`, meshed `10/09/2025` from `07:14:22` to `10:26:53 -0700` in `log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` as confirmed in `CFDME-2025-041_scoping_memo_20251008.docx` §6 and `CFDME-2025-041_Phase1_report_revB.docx` §3.5). By contrast, **`OAS-WUI-01_revD.FCStd`** (adding a `610 mm` parapet above the `2745 mm` wall for a `3355 mm` total height, `50 mm` coping cap, and `25 mm` drip overhang) was not transmitted by Trevor Buckhalter until `10/09/2025 16:12:00 -0700` (`5 hr 45 min` after meshing completed), was never meshed or solved, requires a written Change Order under SOW §8, and departs from the certified `305 mm` test-panel geometry.
     - *Dimensional and Material Alignment Across Four Records*: Across `OAS_wall_assembly_section.png` (Rev A), `OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd`, `RBFMT-25-0918` §2, and `IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` §1.2, the wall consists of two parallel `50 mm` 3D-printed siliceous-aggregate concrete leaves (`20 mm` bead pitch), a `205 mm` uninsulated open-air cavity (no fill, membrane, or fire-stop), an overall thickness of `305 mm` (`50 mm + 205 mm + 50 mm`), continuous horizontal `9-gauge` (`3.8 mm` wire diameter) galvanized steel truss-type (triangular zigzag) ties spaced `600 mm` on center vertically with `25 mm` embedment into each leaf, concrete CHT properties `k = 1.4 W/(m·K)`, `ρ = 2200 kg/m³`, `c_p = 900 J/(kg·K)`, and steel tie CHT properties `k = 45 W/(m·K)` (`ρ = 7850 kg/m³`, `c_p = 490 J/(kg·K)`).

3. **Governing Criterion, Crossing Times, and Section 7 Stub Prediction**:
   - Measured relative to the initial unexposed-face ambient temperature `T_0 = 21.0 °C`:
     - **Single-point temperature-rise criterion (`181 °C` [`325 °F` / `181 K`] rise above `21.0 °C` -> `202.0 °C` surface limit)**: Reached at **`118 min`** in the Red Butte test (`TC-6`, over a `3.8 mm` steel tie course). In `E119_companion_sim_results.csv` (`T_unexposed_max_C`), crossed between `130 min` (`200.5 °C`, `179.5 °C` rise) and `131 min` (`202.1 °C`, `181.1 °C` rise) at **`130.94 min`** (`130.9375 min`), or **`131 min`** to the nearest minute.
     - **Nine-point average temperature-rise criterion (`139 °C` [`250 °F` / `139 K`] rise above `21.0 °C` -> `160.0 °C` surface limit)**: Reached at **`163 min`** in the Red Butte test (`TC-1` through `TC-9` mean). In `E119_companion_sim_results.csv` (`T_unexposed_avg_C`), crossed between `176 min` (`159.9 °C`, `138.9 °C` rise) and `177 min` (`160.9 °C`, `139.9 °C` rise) at **`176.10 min`**, or **`176 min`** to the nearest minute (whereas `177 min` is the integer sample that trips `≥ 160.0 °C`).
   - **Governing Criterion**: Because `131 min < 176 min` in the simulation (and `118 min < 163 min` in the test), the **single-point unexposed-face criterion (`181 °C` / `325 °F` rise above `21.0 °C`, i.e., `202.0 °C`) governs** at **`131 min`**.
   - **Section 7 Stub Prediction**: The prediction **`S = 131 min`** in the Section 7 stub of `CFDME-2025-041_Phase1_report_revB.docx` **stands**.

4. **Adopted Experimental Value `D` and Disposition on Bianca Rennert's `129 min` Figure**:
   - **Adopted Experimental Value**: **`D = 118 min`** from certified Red Butte Report `RBFMT-25-0918` (§5.2–§5.3) and Ironwood Memo `IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` (§2).
   - **Disposition of Bianca's `129 min` Figure**: **Rejected / Inadmissible as `D`** under `CFDME-QA-VAL-002` §6 ("Source of D"). A client-transmitted post-test thermocouple calibration adjustment (`20251009_Rennert_revised_burn_data.eml`, `burn_data_original_vs_revised.csv`) cannot replace `D = 118 min` absent all three required laboratory records: (1) a signed **reissued test report** (`RBFMT-25-0918-R1`) from Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing stating the reason for revision; (2) a traceable **calibration certificate** for `TC-6` supporting the correction (Red Butte's existing certificate `RBFMT-CAL-25-0812-TC`, dated `2025-08-12`, already certified `TC-1` through `TC-10` as NIST-traceable per `SOP-CAL-04` within `90 days` of the `09/24/2025` test); and (3) an **explicit supersession statement** in the reissued report. None of these three records exists.

5. **Error, Acceptance Criterion, Validation Uncertainty, Comparisons, and Maximum Passing Prediction**:
   - **Signed Model Error**: **`E = S − D = 131 min − 118 min = +13 min`** (`+11.02 %` of `D = 118 min`; exact crossing error `+12.94 min` / `+10.96 %`; positive sign retained, indicating non-conservative over-prediction of fire endurance).
   - **Primary Acceptance Criterion (`10 % of D`)**: **`|E| ≤ 11.8 min`** (`10 % × 118 min = 11.8 min`, as the limit falls).
   - **Combined Validation Uncertainty (`u_val`)**: **`u_val = ±9 min`** (root-sum-square of `CFDME-QA-VAL-002` §4 defaults for an E119 CHT wall simulation: `u_num = ±4 min`, `u_inp = ±6 min`, `u_exp = ±5 min` -> `u_val = sqrt((4 min)² + (6 min)² + (5 min)²) = sqrt(77 min²) = ±8.77 min`, reported to the nearest whole minute as `±9 min`).
   - **Comparison Against Both**:
     - *`|E|` vs. Acceptance Criterion (`11.8 min`)*: `|E| = 13 min > 11.8 min` (exceeds limit by `1.2 min`, or `11.02 % > 10.0 %`). **Fails primary acceptance criterion.**
     - *`|E|` vs. Validation Uncertainty (`9 min` / `8.77 min`)*: `|E| = 13 min > 9 min` (exceeds `u_val` by `4 min`, or `4.23 min` against `8.77 min`; `|E| / u_val = 1.44× u_val`). Per `CFDME-QA-VAL-002` §5, the discrepancy sits outside the combined uncertainty floor and is a **resolved systematic model error**.
   - **Largest Prediction That Would Have Cleared the Criterion**: **`129.8 min`** as the limit falls (`118 min + 11.8 min = 129.8 min`; lower bound `106.2 min`), or **`129 min`** when reported to the nearest whole minute (`E = +11 min ≤ 11.8 min`, whereas `130 min` yields `E = +12 min > 11.8 min`).

6. **Two Diagnostic Comparisons, What They Say About the Model, Rework Scope & Status, and Phase 1 Impact**:
   - **Minutes Separating the Two Criteria (`t_avg − t_single`)**:
     - *Test (`RBFMT-25-0918`)*: `163 min − 118 min =` **`45 min`**.
     - *Companion Run (`E119_companion_sim_results.csv`, crossing times to nearest minute)*: `176 min − 131 min =` **`45 min`** (`176.10 min − 130.94 min = 45.16 min` exact; `177 min − 131 min = 46 min` on integer sample trips). Both criteria are delayed by the exact same **`+13 min`**.
   - **How Far the Governing Point Sits Above the Nine-Point Mean at Governance (`T_max − T_avg`)**:
     - *Test at Governance (`t = 118 min`)*: `TC-6` rise is `181 °C` (`202.0 °C`) while the nine-TC mean rise is `96 °C` (`117.0 °C`), so the governing point sits **`85 °C`** (`85.0 °C` / `85.0 K`) above the nine-point mean.
     - *Companion Run at Governance (`t = 131 min` / crossing `130.94 min`)*: At `131 min`, `T_unexposed_max_C = 202.1 °C` (`181.1 °C` rise) while `T_unexposed_avg_C = 110.9 °C` (`89.9 °C` rise), so the governing point sits **`91.2 °C`** (`91.2 K`, or **`91 °C`** to the nearest degree; **`91.17 °C`** at exact crossing `130.94 min`) above the nine-point mean — `+6.2 °C` (`+6 °C`) higher than in the test because the simulated nine-point mean rise at `131 min` (`89.9 °C`) is `6.1 °C` cooler than the test mean rise at `118 min` (`96.0 °C`).
   - **What They Say About the Model & Where Rework Belongs**:
     - Because the tie-to-mean contrast is already strongly captured (`91.2 °C` vs. `85 °C` at governance) and the time lag between single-point failure and nine-point average failure is preserved (`45 min` vs. `45 min`), with *both* curves delayed by `+13 min`, the `+13 min` error is primarily a **uniform, assembly-wide (bulk through-wall) thermal-transmission lag** across the `50 mm` concrete leaves and `205 mm` air cavity, plus secondary local interface discretization at the tie embedment.
     - Rework belongs in: (a) **Through-wall CHT physics & mesh** (`CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf` §§3.4, 3.5, 6 & Appendix A): replacing constant room-temperature solid properties (`k = 1.4 W/(m·K)`, `ρ = 2200 kg/m³`, `c_p = 900 J/(kg·K)` for concrete; `k = 45 W/(m·K)`, `ρ = 7850 kg/m³`, `c_p = 490 J/(kg·K)` for steel ties) with temperature-dependent `k(T), ρ(T), c_p(T)`, auditing furnace-side boundary coupling and `205 mm` cavity `fvDOM` participating radiation (`4` directions / `S4`, `2` bands split at `2.5 μm`, concrete emissivity `0.90 [dimensionless]`, tie emissivity `0.25 [dimensionless]`), and refining the wall/tie mesh (`log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt` currently meshes the `50 mm` leaves at `L6 [dx = 0.0625 m = 62.5 mm]` and ties at `L7 [dx = 0.03125 m = 31.25 mm]`, only `2×` finer than `L6` instead of the mandatory `≥ 4×` refinement at the `25 mm` tie embedments); and (b) **Phase 1 wildfire case setup (`Case/`)**: replacing Mulshi's cross-regime Dry Wash `rhoSimpleFoam` carryover (`OAS_case_setup_from_DWA.txt`) and steady-SIMPLE `k-ε` `fireFoam` run (`controlDict`, `log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt`) with a compliant transient `fireFoam` LES (`WALE` or `Dynamic Smagorinsky` SGS, `atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity`, `EDC` combustion, `fvDOM` radiation, `adjustTimeStep yes`, `maxCo = 0.90 [Courant limit]`, `writeControl adjustableRunTime`) coupled to the 4-region CHT wall mesh.
   - **Whether Any Rework Has Started**: **No.** As of `10/10/2025`, all logs, case files, and validation outputs remain in their `10/09/2025` state, and no rework runs have been started.
   - **Meaning for the Rest of Phase 1**: Section 7 of `CFDME-2025-041_Phase1_report_revB.docx` must report the non-validating rollup (`+13 min ± 9 min`); Ocotillo cannot make a validation claim in its launch deck; and the CHT + transient `fireFoam` LES rework must be completed during Sprint 1–2 (`10/13/2025–10/20/2025`) within the `$84,500` fixed-fee budget before running the six SOW §3.1 production wildfire LES cases (gating Invoice 2 for `$25,350` [`30 %`] on `10/20/2025`), ahead of the `10/27/2025` Red Butte confirmatory test window and `11/07/2025` final Phase 1 delivery (Invoice 3 for `$25,350` [`30 %`]).

7. **Wildfire Claim Scope Limitation, What Closes the Gap, and Future Reporting Form**:
   - **Does / Does Not Establish**: This exercise evaluates only CHT wall response against the standard ASTM E119 post-flashover compartment-fire furnace curve (`RBFMT-25-0918`). Per `CFDME-QA-VAL-002` §7 and `CFDME_Standards_Digest_rev1.pdf` §4, ASTM E119 endurance is a comparative assembly rating, **not** a WUI wildfire exposure (`30.1 MW` over `3.0 m` front segment, `I = 10,040 kW/m`, `5 m/s to 12 m/s` wind at `20 ft`, `Fr = 0.92 to 2.21 [dimensionless]`, `0.87 Hz` / `1.15 s` puffing) and **not** a wildfire survival-time prediction. It does not validate the wildfire LES model, does not establish `2-hour (120 min)` wildfire survival, and does not substantiate Ocotillo's claim of outperforming conventional wood-frame construction in a Sonoran wildfire.
   - **What Closes the Gap**: Reworking the CHT model to validate within `|E| ≤ 11.8 min` on E119, executing the compliant 6-case transient `fireFoam` LES wildfire matrix (verified with `D* = 3.76 m`, `dx = 0.5 m`, `D*/dx = 7.5 cells/D*` [`7.52 cells/D*`], Pope resolved-TKE `84 % ≥ 80 %`), and validating against physical test data representative of the WUI wildfire radiant/convective heat-flux regime (e.g., instrumented testing in the `10/27/2025` Red Butte confirmatory window documented in a certified lab report providing `D`), plus an equivalent benchmark for conventional wood-frame construction.
   - **Mandatory Future Reporting Form**: A single line or table stating **`S`, `D`, `E = S − D` (sign retained), and `u_val = sqrt(u_num² + u_inp² + u_exp²)` in that exact order (`E ± u_val`)**, with every number carrying its unit, citations to the run ID for `S` and certified lab report for `D`, numerical comparison of `|E|` against `10 % of D` and `|E|` against `u_val`, and sign discussion — never a binary `"yes/no"` or `"pass/fail"` label.

8. **Rating Impact of `129 min`, Authority to Act, Stamp Language, and Checklist Disposition**:
   - **Effect on Certified Rating & Authority to Act**: At `D = 118 min`, the assembly fell `2 min` short of the `120 min` (`2-hour`) ASTM E119 threshold and was certified at **1-hour (`60 min`)** (`IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` §3). If `129 min` were ever substantiated (with the average-rise criterion at `163 min`), the assembly would clear `120 min` by `+9 min`, qualifying for upgrade to a **2-hour (`120 min`)** rating (and yielding `E = +2 min ≤ 12.9 min` against `S = 131 min`). Only **Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing** (by issuing a signed reissued test report `RBFMT-25-0918-R1` with a traceable `TC-6` calibration certificate and supersession statement) and **Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering** (**Marla Kettering, PE, `AZ PE #45106`**, by issuing a new certification memorandum superseding `IWFPE-CERT-25-0374`) are entitled to act (`IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` §4).
   - **Mandatory Stamp Language (`CFDME-QA-VAL-002` §9)**:
     > `"CFD thermal analysis only. Fire-resistance rating certified separately by others."`
   - **Peer-Review Checklist Disposition (`CFDME-2025-041_peer_review_checklist.docx`)**:
     - **Item Closed by This Memo**: **Item 6** (*Validation reported as `E ± u_val` against acceptance criterion, NOT yes/no, per Validation Procedure rev 2 §§3–5*). (Items **1** and **8** were already closed `[X]`.)
     - **Items Staying Open**: **Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, and 10** remain `[ ] OPEN` on the Phase 1 report checklist (with Section 2 of this memo supplying the complete timestamp/hash verification evidence to close **Item 7** once transcribed into Report §3.5, while Items **2, 3, 4, 5, 9, and 10** await case-setup rework, moving `D*/dx = 7.5 cells/D*` and `84 %` Pope resolved-TKE from Appendix C into the Section 6 Verification body, correcting the `psf`-to-`Pa` conversion defect [`+12.4 psf = +594 Pa`, `−7.8 psf = −372 Pa`, `−10.86 psf = −520 Pa` at `96 mph` / `42.9 m/s`] and cross-case wind check, and final reviewer sign-off).

---

### Ready-to-Send Paragraph for Bianca Rennert Today (`10/10/2025`)

> "Bianca — We have completed our formal ASME V&V 20 validation review of the ASTM E119 companion simulation for the 305 mm double-wythe printed-concrete wall assembly (OAS-WUI-01_revC / Drawing OAS-WA-305mm-DW Rev A: two 50 mm concrete leaves, a 205 mm uninsulated air cavity, and 9-gauge [3.8 mm] galvanized steel truss ties at 600 mm vertical spacing with 25 mm embedment), and we cannot describe the simulation as 'validated against the certified test' in Ocotillo's launch materials. Under our firm's Validation QA Procedure (CFDME-QA-VAL-002, rev 2), validation is reported quantitatively as the signed model error E = S − D with its combined validation uncertainty u_val rather than a yes/no verdict, and the experimental reference D must be taken from the signed third-party laboratory report of record (Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing Report RBFMT-25-0918, dated 09/24/2025, and Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering Certification Memorandum IWFPE-CERT-25-0374, dated 09/29/2025). For the governing single-point unexposed-face criterion (181 °C [325 °F] temperature rise above the 21.0 °C initial ambient temperature, or 202.0 °C surface temperature), our companion simulation predicts a crossing time of S = 131 min (with the 139 °C [250 °F] nine-point average-rise limit of 160.0 °C crossed at 176 min) against the certified experimental single-point endurance of D = 118 min at thermocouple TC-6 (nine-point average reached at 163 min), yielding a signed model error of E = S − D = +13 min (+11.02 % of D) and a combined validation uncertainty of u_val = ±9 min (±8.77 min root-sum-square from u_num = ±4 min, u_inp = ±6 min, and u_exp = ±5 min), or E ± u_val = +13 min ± 9 min. Because |E| = 13 min exceeds both our 10 % acceptance criterion of 11.8 min (10 % × 118 min, under which the largest passing prediction would have been 129.8 min, or 129 min to the nearest minute) and u_val = 9 min, the +13 min over-prediction is a resolved model error requiring through-wall CHT model rework ahead of our Sprint 2 (10/20/2025) runs and the 10/27/2025 Red Butte confirmatory window. We cannot adopt the client-revised 129 min figure in burn_data_original_vs_revised.csv unless Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing issues a formally signed, reissued test report (e.g., RBFMT-25-0918-R1) accompanied by a NIST-traceable calibration certificate for TC-6 and an explicit supersession statement replacing 118 min with 129 min; moreover, while a substantiated 129 min endurance would clear the 120 min threshold for a 2-hour rating by 9 min (up from the current certified 1-hour [60 min] rating), only Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering (Marla Kettering, PE, AZ PE #45106) has authority to reissue or upgrade the certified fire-resistance rating once backed by a reissued Red Butte report. Finally, please note for your counsel and press deck that an ASTM E119 furnace comparison evaluates comparative compartment-fire endurance only — it does not validate wildfire performance or predict survival time in a Sonoran Desert WUI wildfire — and our PE stamp covers 'CFD thermal analysis only. Fire-resistance rating certified separately by others.'"
